title: Quasi-finite at a point implies isolated in the fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ with first projection $p:X_s\to X$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite], then the unique point $\xi\in X_s$ with $p(\xi)=x$ is isolated in $X_s$: $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$. Equivalently, $\{x\}$ is open in the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), (1) implies (2).)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, first paragraph of the proof ((1) implies (2)); Definition 01TD (definition-quasi-finite), line 3538

proof.text: Unpack IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint [pqf-def-quasifinite] into affine opens U, V, the appLE algebra, its finite-type witness, and IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] at q = hU.primeIdealOf x. Transport the open singleton through PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], obtaining an open singleton in the set-theoretic affine fibre. Mathlib Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.of_isOpen_singleton_fiber then gives Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q.asIdeal.

Use Mathlib IsAffineOpen.arrowStalkMapIso on U and V [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and RingHom.QuasiFinite.respectsIso.arrow_mk_iso_iff to reduce Scheme.Hom.QuasiFiniteAt f x to quasi-finiteness of Localization.localRingHom. Its composite with R -> R_p is R -> A_q, by Localization.localRingHom_to_map and the scalar tower. Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q supplies quasi-finiteness of this composite; RingHom.QuasiFinite.of_comp supplies quasi-finiteness of the local ring map.

Apply Mathlib Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber to obtain openness of {f.asFiber x}. The locally-of-finite-type hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis of this Mathlib theorem. Transport this open singleton by f.fiberHomeo (f x) [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; asFiber is its inverse applied to <x,rfl>, so its image is the required singleton in the set-theoretic fibre.
